items.title: A finite module whose k-th Fitting ideal is principal is generated by k elements after removing its f-torsion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a finite module over a local ring whose k-th Fitting ideal is generated by one element f, the quotient by the f-torsion is generated by k elements, and the proof is a 27-line matrix argument. It chooses a surjection from a free module, uses Nakayama to replace a generating set of the Fitting ideal by a single minor of the relation matrix, constructs a right inverse for the relation matrix up to the factor f, and then exhibits n - k explicit combinations of the chosen generators that are killed by f; since the remaining n - k generators already generate the module modulo those combinations, the quotient by the f-torsion is generated by k elements. The Nakayama step and the construction of the annihilated combinations are the content, and both are displayed.
